sources.title: NPR Topics: Home Page Top Stories

articles.author: Claudia Grisales
articles.description: The vote on a war powers resolution introduced by Democrats came at a moment when some Republicans have begun to distance themselves from President Trump over the ongoing conflict.
articles.title: In one of their last votes before November, Senate GOP blocks effort to end Iran war

articles.author: Tonya Mosley
articles.description: Rolling Stone reporter Cheyenne Roundtree says rumors of abuse followed the media mogul for years. Her book examines how Combs remained so powerful, despite decades of warning signs and allegations.
articles.title: 'Bad Boy For Life' investigates the culture that enabled Sean Combs' alleged abuse

articles.author: Justin Chang
articles.description: It's not easy, killing people and raising a family. The new action-thriller Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother reaffirms the power of faith — and delights in outrageous juxtapositions.
articles.title: Mahershala Ali stars as a devout father of three, making ends meet as a hitman

articles.author: Sydney Lupkin
articles.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s annual financial disclosure reveals he has received two lucrative book advances and free flights from a friend while in office.
articles.title: RFK Jr.'s ethics filing reveals book deals worth millions of dollars

articles.author: Stephan Bisaha
articles.description: Rates have climbed more than a full percentage point since the U.S. war against Iran started.
articles.title: Mortgage rates have just surpassed 7% for the first time in well over a year

articles.author: Jennifer Ludden
articles.description: Despite lower poverty overall, the rate for seniors has been steadily rising in recent years. A new AARP survey sheds light on how those over 50 are struggling in the crucial time before retirement.
articles.title: The economic squeeze is pushing up poverty rates for older adults

articles.author: Dhanika Pineda
articles.description: Set in the same universe as Tahir's Ember in Ashes series, Empire picks up right where the last book, 'Heir' left off — with S'rsha attached to the very monster she sought to destroy.
articles.title: 'Empire' asks: When a child dies, who pays the price?

articles.author: Rob Schmitz
articles.description: Despite the pageantry and the cordial tone, expectations for any big breakthroughs on issues ranging from AI to Iran to a trade war truce are low.
articles.title: Trump and Xi strike cordial tone at summit amid underlying tensions

articles.author: Fatma Tanis
articles.description: In Liberia, joint financial planning boosted cash aid's benefits. It also had an unexpected consequence for some families.
articles.title: Needy couples got cash and a spending plan. Results were good -- and bad

articles.author: Joseph Kim
articles.description: Stories of science funding being cut, labs shutting down and scientists losing jobs have flooded the media under Trump's administration. These six graphics show how those changes have affected U.S. biomedical research.
articles.title: These 6 charts show how NIH research funding has been reshaped under Trump

articles.author: Nick Visser
articles.description:
Follow the day’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

AI hack of Medicare exposes Australia’s vulnerabilities
Technology experts have warned revelations an artificial intelligence agent hacked Medicare’s internal systems will not be the only dangerous breach of government data and have called for Australia to boost its protections against the growing risk.
Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them.
What if it was a less benign breach? What if it was a less benign actor? Let’s face it, clearly, Services Australia’s cybersecurity is woefully inadequate.
I mean the irony here is that you actually need AI to fight AI. This should hasten, if anything, our move over in the US to less finger wagging and Trump one-upmanship, and more about embracing these AI companies and bringing them here so that we can have frontier models providing sovereign capability to Australia. Because AI is going to happen.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: PM says he learned of OpenAI’s Medicare breach in New York; NSW renters to benefit from new laws

articles.author: Kat Wong
articles.description:
Beau Lamarre-Condon, 31, has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Paddington terrace in early 2024

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Beau Lamarre-Condon asked a friend, “What would you do if I told you I killed somebody?” nine months before allegedly murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies, a Sydney court has heard.
The New South Wales police officer then assured the friend he hadn’t killed anyone, before admitting he had entered Baird’s house while he was away, before stealing a Polaroid camera and eating an Easter egg.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW cop asked friend ‘what would you do if I told you I killed somebody’ before alleged murders, court told

articles.author: Australian Associated Press
articles.description:
The marked police car was travelling with its sirens on when it hit a tree in inner-city Sydney about 1.30am on Friday

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A New South Wales police officer who was killed on duty when the car she was travelling in crashed into a tree in Sydney has been named as 20-year-old Mia Lay.
NSW police said the marked police car was travelling under lights and sirens along Gibbons Street in Redfern when it crashed at about 1.30am on Friday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NSW police officer killed ‘instantly’ after car she was travelling in crashed into tree in Redfern

articles.author: Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
A TV spot claims the US president is trying to sway October’s presidential vote in favour of Lula’s far-right opponents
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s presidential campaign has accused Donald Trump of wanting to “colonise” Brazil in order to capture its natural resources by meddling in next month’s presidential election.
The accusation came in a televised campaign advert that was broadcast on Thursday by Lula’s team amid growing fears over the impact alleged US interference could have on the vote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula says Trump wants to ‘colonise’ and capture Brazil’s resources by meddling in election

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
The ⁠Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said the missiles were ⁠aimed at Taif and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea, the main alternative route for Saudi oil
Saudi Arabia says it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis, with the latest attacks pushing oil prices ⁠to a one-week high over fears of spiralling supply disruptions.
The ⁠Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said the missiles were ⁠aimed at Taif in western Saudi ​Arabia and the Yanbu area on the Red Sea, with the Houthis claiming their attacks were aimed at “a sensitive target” in the capital Riyadh and on Saudi Aramco facilities in Tanbu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts wave of Houthi missiles as oil climbs to one-week high

articles.author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
articles.description:
Email to members says money lent to a party-linked company to establish a micro distillery

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has admitted using party funds to build a $56,000 shed on James Ashby’s private property.
Guardian Australia revealed on Monday that a company linked to One Nation – Small Batch Brewing Pty Ltd – was the purchaser of the shed on Ashby’s property despite having no revenue stream and not being licensed to make or sell alcohol.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: One Nation admits using party funds to build $56,000 shed on James Ashby’s private property

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Marina Dunbar and Chris Hippensteel
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

CNN and MS Now journalists denied access to White House state dinner despite court ruling

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Lawyers for the news outlets President Trump banned from the White House have requested an emergency hearing after several journalists were turned away from the building Thursday morning, in apparent defiance of a federal judge’s order to restore their access.
“This morning journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO attempted to enter the White House and were turned away, and Secret Service agents confiscated the hard pass of journalists whose hard passes had not previously been confiscated,” a new court filing read.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s state dinner for Xi Jinping will not be televised as White House continues to deny CNN full access – as it happened

articles.author: Jeremy Barr in Washington and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Officials deny entry even after federal judge rules Trump administration must grant banned journalists access
Journalists for CNN and MS Now were denied access to the White House state dinner in honor of Xi Jinping, China’s president, on Thursday evening, hours after a federal judge ruled the Trump administration must allow them in after imposing a ban last week.
“About an hour before Xi’s arrival was scheduled, the White House said CNN could cover the event, but only with a photojournalist and audio technician, notably excluding the network’s editorial team consisting of a reporter and producer,” CNN reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN and MS Now journalists denied access to White House state dinner despite court ruling

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Mikie Sherrill says Dale Caldwell ‘engaged in serious, repeated violations’ involving staffers and gifts
New Jersey’s governor on Thursday called on the state’s lieutenant governor, Dale Caldwell, to resign by Friday after a law firm hired by her office concluded he violated the state’s ethics and discrimination rules.
The report published Wednesday found that Caldwell violated the state’s policy prohibiting discrimination in the workplace. It said he made an advance toward a staffer’s friend and when he was rebuffed, he told the staffer: “You young women are looking for young sperm.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New Jersey governor calls on lieutenant governor to resign after ethics investigation

articles.author: Robert Tait in Washington
articles.description:
Chinese president’s proposals for lessening tensions come amid period of intense competition between the two countries over AI and trade
Xi Jinping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course amid rising tensions over artificial intelligence, trade and Taiwan.
At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could steer the two competing superpowers away from future military conflict and on to a road of mutual gain.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
James Copenhaver, 76, left with lingering injuries after gunman opened fire from rooftop at 2024 Pennsylvania rally
James Copenhaver, one of three campaign rally attendees shot in 2024 during an assassination attempt on then candidate Donald Trump, has died in Pittsburgh, his lawyer said Thursday. He was 76.
Copenhaver was in the bleachers during the event in Butler, Pennsylvania, when a 20-year-old gunman opened fire from a nearby rooftop, grazing Trump’s right ear with one bullet. Copenhaver was struck in the arm and in the abdomen, wounds that left him with lingering injuries and walking with a cane.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Man shot and wounded during Trump assassination attempt in Butler dies

articles.author: Alice Speri and Lex McMenamin
articles.description:
Actor Susan Sarandon, whistleblower Chelsea Manning and comedian Caleb Hearon are detained by NYPD
More than 100 people were arrested outside the United Nations’ headquarters in New York City on Thursday as Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the general assembly, a speech that also prompted dozens of UN delegates to walk out in protest.
The protest outside the UN, one of several this week against the embattled Israeli prime minister, drew hundreds of Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian and Lebanese New Yorkers, among others, as well as several elected officials and candidates in the November election, and a number of celebrities.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’

articles.author: Guardian staff and agencies
articles.description:
Actors detained at Jewish Voice for Peace demonstration against Israeli prime minister’s address to the UN general assembly
Oscar-winning actor Susan Sarandon and Hacks star Hannah Einbinder were among people detained by police in New York on Thursday as they moved in to break up a protest against Benjamin Netanyahu.
Agence France-Presse footage shows NYPD officers cuffing Thelma & Louise star Sarandon at the demo in the city as the Israeli prime minister was readying to address the United Nations general assembly.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Susan Sarandon and Hannah Einbinder arrested at anti-Netanyahu protest in New York

articles.author: Martin Farrer
articles.description:
The 11-year-old died at Westmead children’s hospital three days after incident at a unit in Norwest

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A boy who was allegedly shot at a home in Sydney’s north-west earlier this week has died.
Police said that the boy, who had been in a critical condition since being found with a gunshot wound at a unit in Norwest on Monday, died in hospital at about 8pm on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Boy, 11, shot in the face and neck in Sydney dies from his injuries

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Industry leaders call on government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security
The gap between Britain’s food and drink exports and imports has neared its highest this century, as a combination of Brexit, war in the Middle East and US tariffs dented deliveries overseas while imports soared.
The UK’s food and drink trade deficit has risen to more than £21bn – the largest since 2000 – in what industry leaders said was a “wake-up call” for the government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK food and drink trade deficit largest since 2000 at £21bn

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in New York
articles.description:
Country says US must lift sanctions on its oil exports and end the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon
Iran said it has told Donald Trump it is willing to open the strait of Hormuz in six days, and to start talks on its nuclear program the day after, so long as the US lifts sanctions on Iran’s oil exports in return, ends the war on all fronts – including in Lebanon – and releases some of Iran’s frozen assets.
The proposal is designed to accelerate the steps first laid down in the memorandum of understanding signed by the US and Iran in June, particularly by helping the talks on Iran’s nuclear program start much more quickly than previously agreed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran awaiting response from Trump on proposal to open strait of Hormuz in six days

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators 
Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise.
Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer

articles.author: Amelia Gentleman and Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Thirty-seven-year-old charged with one count of criminal damage and failing to disclose his phone pin to police 
The far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been charged with criminal damage and failing to disclose his phone pin to police following an incident in the Channel on Tuesday, where he allegedly slashed a dinghy while a French rescuer was on board.
Thomas, 37, of no fixed abode, has been charged with one count of criminal damage along with an offence under section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (Ripa), for allegedly failing to comply with a notice to disclose a phone pin to police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right activist Daniel Thomas charged over alleged dinghy slashing in Channel

articles.author: Anna Bawden and Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Patient groups decry ‘scandalous’ delays as four integrated care boards take step due to soaring demand for diagnoses
NHS bodies are forcing people with suspected attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism to wait at least two years before they can be assessed as they struggle to meet surging demand for diagnoses of neurodiversity.
Four NHS integrated care boards (ICBs) covering large regions of England have adopted the approach because they cannot afford the cost of the number of assessments that people are seeking.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS bodies in England impose two-year minimum wait for ADHD and autism assessments

articles.author: PA Media
articles.description:
Officers left feeling ‘hamstrung’, says Mark Rowley after offender allowed to return to flat overlooking playground
Pressure to cut the number of prisoners on remand has led to “dangerous and prolific offenders” being granted bail, the country’s most senior police officer said after a paedophile was allowed to return to his flat that overlooked a children’s playground.
Zafer Dogan was jailed on Thursday for two years and four months after he was convicted of taking thousands of pictures of women and girls before using AI technology to turn them into nude images for his sexual gratification.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Met chief criticises court system after paedophile granted bail

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Deference was deafening as US president rolled out red carpet for world’s biggest jailer of journalists – perhaps he was seeking tips
One is an authoritarian who represses the media and has a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.
Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?

articles.author: Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
Legislators sent letter to Marco Rubio saying US interference is weakening  Brazil’s democratic institutions

US politics live – latest updates

A group of 31 Democratic members of the US Congress has sent a letter to the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, criticising the Trump administration over “an apparent effort to interfere with, and potentially undermine” Brazil’s elections.
Latin America’s largest country will hold the first round of its presidential election on 4 October, with polls showing a technical tie between the incumbent leftist president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, and the far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Democratic lawmakers accuse Trump administration of interference in Brazilian elections

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Monthly ‘thank you’ payments for people hosting refugees to be cut from £350 to £100 from next year
Ukrainian refugees in the UK fear they could be left homeless after the government quietly axed 70% of funding for hosts of the Homes for Ukraine scheme, reducing monthly “thank you” payments to them from £350 to £100.
The scheme was launched after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has provided support for 181,000 of the 234,000 Ukrainians who have since sought sanctuary in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukrainians in UK fear homelessness over host scheme funding cuts

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
‘If you’re not in the internal market, you don’t get the same protection,’ says French minister of policy designed to curb Chinese competition
France is leading a push to exclude the UK from the EU’s “Made in Europe” policy that could result in British companies losing out in the race to supply European countries with low-carbon technologies and electric cars.
The plans were raised by Andy Burnham when he met the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, on the sidelines of the UN general assembly earlier this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France says EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ law should not include the UK

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Datacentre hailed by government was supposed to start operating next year but may be held back into mid-2030s
A huge datacentre project hailed by the UK government will miss its launch date next year and could be delayed into the mid-2030s.
The site in Loughton, Essex, was described as the country’s largest AI supercomputer when it was announced in 2025, but power supply problems mean it now faces a lengthy wait before coming online.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Launch of UK’s ‘largest AI supercomputer’ delayed by power supply problems

articles.author: Pjotr Sauer in Kyiv
articles.description:
Warning comes hours after Poland says fire at Starlink satellite station was ‘act of sabotage’
Russia could launch a limited military attack against a Nato country in the coming months, Danish intelligence said, in one of the starkest warnings yet by western security services.
In a report published on Thursday, the Danish defence intelligence service warned of a “low but growing risk” that Russia could launch long-range strikes on Nato infrastructure supporting Ukraine, or carry out a limited incursion into a neighbouring country with a small number of troops, potentially operating without insignia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russia could attack a Nato country within months, Danish intelligence says

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Former Yes musician plays at sanctuary to raise awareness of animals that remain stuck in cages at ‘bile farms’ 
Rick Wakeman has played to all kinds of people around the globe, but he has now performed to an audience he had never encountered before – an enclosure of 150 bears.
The former Yes musician, who has gone on to have a prolific solo career, played the piano at a Vietnamese bear sanctuary.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rick Wakeman performs piano concert to 150 rescued moon bears in Vietnam

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi and agencies
articles.description:
Fighting escalates after Tigrayan rebels form new coalition aimed at overthrowing Abiy Ahmed government
There are growing fears of a return to civil war in Ethiopia after an offensive by fighters from Tigray into the neighbouring states of Afar and Amhara and the formation of a new rebel alliance aimed at overthrowing the government of the prime minister, Abiy Ahmed.
About 600,000 people died between 2020 and 2022 during a devastating war between the Ethiopian army and the political party and paramilitary group the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF). Both sides are now accusing the other of triggering a return to open conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rebel offensive against Ethiopian army stokes fears of return to civil war

articles.author: Kate Connolly in Berlin
articles.description:
Man accused of being accessory to murders at Stalag 326 VI K amid race to prosecute suspects before they die
A 105-year-old man is under investigation on suspicion of being an accessory to multiple murders at a Nazi prisoner of war camp, German prosecutors have said.
The case, which is being handled by the public prosecutor’s office in Dortmund, centres on the Stalag 326 VI K camp in western Germany, in what is now the state of North Rhine-Westphalia.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Germany investigates 105-year-old suspected former Nazi prison camp guard

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Taraneh and Romina Rahimi were charged with ‘waging war against God’ after joining protests against Tehran regime
The family of 21-year-old twins who have been sentenced respectively to death and decades in jail for protesting against the Iranian regime have appealed to the United Nations for help.
A formal “submission of information” relating to the case of Taraneh and Romina Rahimi has been submitted by British human right lawyers on their family’s behalf.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Family of Iranian twins sentenced to death and decades in jail ask UN for help

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.author: Catherine Shoard  and Lorenzo Tondo
articles.description:
Theatrical rollout across 56 territories planned for documentary about Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza before film will stream on Guardian website
NAZA, the award-winning documentary from Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is set to be released in cinemas in more than 50 countries before a digital global release on theguardian.com.
The film, which the Guardian produced, premiered at the Venice film festival earlier this month, where it was met with a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Global release announced for acclaimed Gaza documentary NAZA

articles.author: Lisa O’Carroll
articles.description:
Explosive growth in imported vehicles omitted from EV tariffs fuels concern for future of European carmakers

EU imports three times more from China than bloc exports there

Sales of Chinese hybrid cars have rocketed in the EU in the past four and a half years, data shows, underlining growing concerns in Brussels over the future of the European car industry.
In 2022, just 659 Chinese-made fully hybrid cars (vehicles in which the petrol or diesel engine charge the motor and battery) were sold in the EU. However, after Brussels imposed anti-subsidy tariffs on fully electric cars from China in 2024, sales of hybrids have shot up to 160,662 in the first seven months of this year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alarm bells sound in Brussels as EU sales of Chinese hybrid cars rocket

articles.author: Ariana Baio in Washington
articles.description:
President lays out red carpet as treasury secretary announces extension of ‘Busan agreement’ pausing trade war hostilities

AI, trade, Taiwan and climate: what will and won’t be on agenda at Trump-Xi summit

Donald Trump has welcomed Xi Jinping to the US, taking the unusual step of greeting the Chinese leader on the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews to kick off his state visit to Washington.
Xi’s plane was met with a lavish arrival ceremony that included a 30-metre-long (100ft) red carpet flanked by US service members, a military flyover by two B-1 bombers and a presentation of the flags and national anthems of both countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump greets Xi Jinping on arrival in rare move as US-China trade truce extended

articles.author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
articles.description:
Argentinian president accuses United Nations of being filled with ‘parasites’ in bellicose general assembly speech
Javier Milei has condemned the UN as he warned that Argentina would take “matters into our own hands” in its dispute with Britain over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.
In a caustic speech at the general assembly in New York, the Argentinian president criticised the UN for being ineffective when it came to the long-running tensions over the British overseas territory in the south Atlantic known in Argentina as the Malvinas.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Milei threatens at UN that Argentina will take ‘matters into our own hands’ on Falklands

articles.author: Tom Phillips Latin America correspondent
articles.description:
Venezuela’s interim president hails ‘historic meeting’ and does not say whether she will visit snatched predecessor
Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, has celebrated a “historic” meeting with Donald Trump in New York, posing for a smiley photo with the US president, less than nine months after he ordered the abduction of her boss, Nicolás Maduro.
The former foes met at a five-star hotel a few blocks from Trump Tower in Manhattan late on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN general assembly. The hotel is about 7 miles from the Brooklyn prison where Maduro has been held since he was snatched during a special forces raid on Caracas in January.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Delcy Rodríguez poses with Trump in New York as Maduro languishes in jail nearby

articles.author: Joanna Partridge
articles.description:
Sunil Bharti Mittal’s Airtel Money targets $9bn IPO in boost for ailing UK stock market
Nils Pratley: Does this mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet
A payments business that operates across Africa and is ultimately controlled by an Indian billionaire has announced its intention to float on the struggling London Stock Exchange.
Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa, is planning one of the biggest UK listings in years, in a boost for the shrinking London market that has faced a string of recent departures.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

articles.author: Rachel Savage in Johannesburg
articles.description:
Arrest of Shadrack Sibiya comes as country reels from cases of femicide and alleged police corruption and criminality
One of South Africa’s most senior police officers has been charged with raping an 18-year-old woman and grooming a 16-year-old girl, as the country’s police face allegations of corruption and failing to tackle violence against women and girls.
Shadrack Sibiya, who was already suspended from his role as deputy national police commissioner over allegations he interfered with political killings investigations, was arrested on Monday. He is facing charges of rape, people trafficking, promoting the sexual grooming of a child and two counts of grooming a child.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Top South African police officer charged with raping woman, 18, and grooming 16-year-old girl

articles.author: Natricia Duncan Caribbean correspondent
articles.description:
The move comes after Jamaica’s culture minister Olivia Grange travelled to the UK earlier this month to lodge the historic petition
King Charles has referred a landmark slavery reparations petition from Jamaica to a high-level UK appeals court for legal advice, Jamaica’s culture minister announced in parliament on Tuesday.
Referring to the move as a “really big deal”, Olivia Grange told Jamaica’s MPs the monarch had confirmed that their legal questions have been passed on to the London-based privy council – the final court of appeal for UK overseas territories and some Commonwealth countries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Jamaica hails King’s decision to refer slavery reparations petition to privy council as ‘really big deal’

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Islamic State-inspired bombings of churches and hotels in 2019 was one of the country’s worst ever attacks
A court in Sri Lanka has convicted 15 men on terrorist charges for their involvement in the deadly 2019 Easter bombings and sentenced them each to at least 220 years in prison.
The terror attacks, which targeted luxury hotels and churches as they held Easter services, left 267 people dead and wounded almost 600. The bombings, which were inspired by Islamic State (IS), were among the deadliest terror attacks in Sri Lanka’s history and sent shockwaves through the country.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Sri Lanka Easter bombings: 15 sentenced to hundreds of years in prison each over deadly terror attacks

articles.author: Niha Masih
articles.description:
Generations of artisans from Mumbai to Lucknow have shaped the world’s most coveted designs. Plus, the gen Z memes giving classic Bollywood a new life
The zardozi embroidery on a Dior dress, the T-strap leather sandals at a Prada show, the mirror-work technique used on a Fendi bag – for decades, the skill of Indian artisans has been an invisible force behind some of the world’s most coveted fashion.
Now, that work is beginning to claim its own place in the spotlight, and the Mumbai-based textile and embroidery atelier Chanakya International is at the forefront.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘What we have is unique’: the Indian craftsmanship behind global luxury fashion

articles.author: Tobi Thomas health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Accra Reset’s report states countries in the region and global south should take greater control of their health development after USAID debacle
The United States’ withdrawal from key aid programs has put healthcare in Africa and the global south “under growing strain” a new report warns.
The report says the Trump administration’s cuts to programs such as US Agency for International Development (USAID), as well as the Covid-19 pandemic and rising costs of living globally have brought “new urgency” for the need to reform healthcare in the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthcare in Africa ‘under growing strain’ after US withdrawal from aid programs, report warns

articles.author: Shah Meer Baloch in Islamabad and Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Police crack down on family and political supporters of former PM who say authorities are ‘slowly killing’ him in prison
Three sisters of Pakistan’s incarcerated former prime minister Imran Khan have been arrested amid a heavy-handed government crackdown on plans for a nationwide protest to demand Khan’s release.
The lawyer for the three sisters, Aleema Khan, Uzma Khan and Noreen Niazi, said on Monday that they had all been detained and jailed for 30 days under a warrant that accused them of being a threat to public order.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pakistan jails sisters of Imran Khan before protest seeking his release

articles.author: Louisa Loveluck
articles.description:
After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. An in-depth investigation reveals the ‘show of force’ costing American taxpayers millions
No one would tell the shackled detainees onboard the US immigration plane where they were going. The officers in charge would taunt them when they asked, they said. It was only when the seat-back video screens finally showed a map that the 18 migrants worked it out.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Banished to alien lands: Trump’s secret deportation deals

articles.author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
articles.description:
Jagtar Singh Johal, from Scotland, was arrested after wedding in Punjab on alleged terrorism offences
Jagtar Singh Johal, a British Sikh man who was arrested in India in 2017 in connection with alleged terrorism offences, has been granted bail by a Delhi court.
Johal, from Scotland, was arrested for his alleged role in funding the Khalistan Liberation Force, which had carried out targeted killings in India’s Punjab region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Sikh man granted bail in India nine years after arrest

articles.author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland, with Shrai Popat, produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic, and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
This week, the US press corps stood up to Donald Trump after he banned three organisations he doesn’t like from the White House. But when it came to the leader of one of America’s oldest adversaries – China – well, Trump literally rolled out a very long red carpet.
Jonathan Freedland speaks to the Guardian’s Shrai Popat about why Trump seems weaker these days, and why it might be dangerous to underestimate him

articles.author: Tom Phillips and Tiago Rogero in Rio de Janeiro
articles.description:
A TV spot claims the US president is trying to sway October’s presidential vote in favour of Lula’s far-right opponents
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s presidential campaign has accused Donald Trump of wanting to “colonise” Brazil in order to capture its natural resources by meddling in next month’s presidential election.
The accusation came in a televised campaign advert that was broadcast on Thursday by Lula’s team amid growing fears over the impact alleged US interference could have on the vote.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Lula says Trump wants to ‘colonise’ and capture Brazil’s resources by meddling in election

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Marina Hyde; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Laurence Topham and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Guardian columnist Marina Hyde on the release of her new book What a Time to be Alive!
“I think increasingly the way to survive the news is to say things like: ‘I find it fascinating from a human behaviour point of view,’” says Marina Hyde. “It’s like a firewall against actually thinking: ‘My God, I mean, what are we living through?’”
On the publication of her new book, What a Time to Be Alive!, The Guardian’s award-winning columnist talks to Nosheen Iqbal about Donald Trump, AI, Taylor Swift’s wedding … and her chance, tragic encounter with Keir Starmer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Marina Hyde on Trump, tech bros and Taylor Swift - podcast

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Marina Dunbar and Chris Hippensteel
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

CNN and MS Now journalists denied access to White House state dinner despite court ruling

Sign up for US Breaking News emails

Lawyers for the news outlets President Trump banned from the White House have requested an emergency hearing after several journalists were turned away from the building Thursday morning, in apparent defiance of a federal judge’s order to restore their access.
“This morning journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO attempted to enter the White House and were turned away, and Secret Service agents confiscated the hard pass of journalists whose hard passes had not previously been confiscated,” a new court filing read.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s state dinner for Xi Jinping will not be televised as White House continues to deny CNN full access – as it happened

articles.author: Jeremy Barr in Washington and Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Officials deny entry even after federal judge rules Trump administration must grant banned journalists access
Journalists for CNN and MS Now were denied access to the White House state dinner in honor of Xi Jinping, China’s president, on Thursday evening, hours after a federal judge ruled the Trump administration must allow them in after imposing a ban last week.
“About an hour before Xi’s arrival was scheduled, the White House said CNN could cover the event, but only with a photojournalist and audio technician, notably excluding the network’s editorial team consisting of a reporter and producer,” CNN reported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN and MS Now journalists denied access to White House state dinner despite court ruling

articles.author: David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Deference was deafening as US president rolled out red carpet for world’s biggest jailer of journalists – perhaps he was seeking tips
One is an authoritarian who represses the media and has a strong allergy to democratic elections. The other is head of the Chinese Communist party.
Donald Trump welcomed the Chinese president, Xi Jinping, to the White House on Thursday, setting the stage for a scene quite unlike anything the august old building has seen over more than two centuries.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump swoons over strongman soulmate Xi – are you feeling jealous, Vladimir?

articles.author: Guardian Staff
articles.description:
CNN senior reporter Betsy Klein gained access to the White House on 24 September, hours after a federal judge ruled against Donald Trump's media ban. The ban had barred reporters from CNN, MS Now and Politico from accessing the White House
 Continue reading...
articles.title: CNN reporter arrives at White House after judge rules against Trump's media ban – video

articles.author: Moira Donegan
articles.description:
Conservatives long promoted a politics of sexual prohibition. Now such morals have been shed in favor of male domination
Under Kash Patel, the FBI will now hire you even if you have a history of hiring prostitutes, or of having sex with animals. The rightwing Maha influencer Alex Clark had a guest on to her talk show to discuss the idea that wives should provide sex for their husbands on demand. A new ad for a sports gambling website is being hailed as a victory for the political right, because it features a nude Sydney Sweeney clutching footballs to her breasts. The Tate brothers, who encourage their male followers to pursue compulsive sexual conquest and who have been accused of sex trafficking and violence in the operation of their online cam porn business, have reportedly been friendly with members of Trump’s circle. A dizzying array of elites on both sides of the aisle – conservatives very much included – seem to have been socializing with a pedophile financier, and were so unfazed by his constant coterie of underaged girl companions that one begins to wonder whether they were habituated to such scenes. A prominent conservative writer, best known for her opposition to gender transition care for children, has announced a new book claiming to tackle the problem of young women who are supposedly unwilling to have enough sex. And the women of the president’s members club, Mar-A-Lago, are so well known for their dramatic facelifts, and their lips so stuffed with filler that they cannot quite close their mouths, that their faces are now a shorthand in the world of plastic surgery.
Raunch, vulgarity, a boorish entitlement to women’s sexual service, and the aesthetics – and, indeed, the business – of pornography are being embraced by the right.
Moira Donegan is a Guardian US columnist
 Continue reading...
articles.title: In its push to subordinate women, the American right is embracing raunch

articles.author: Kenneth Roth
articles.description:
It is sad and dangerous that at such a perilous moment, the United States is saddled with a president like Trump
Donald Trump’s speech on Tuesday to the United Nations general assembly was an object lesson in his lawless rule and remarkable capacity for self-delusion. Disregarding the UN charter’s emphasis on the peaceful resolution of disputes, he doubled down on his violent unilateralism while denigrating the global issues that the UN is designed to address.
For many, the headline remark was his musing about whether to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” of Iran. “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations?”
Kenneth Roth is a Guardian US columnist, a senior fellow at Yale University and a former executive director of Human Rights Watch. He is the author of Righting Wrongs: Three Decades on the Front Lines Battling Abusive Governments
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump’s UN speech was delusional and dangerous | Kenneth Roth

articles.author: Ed Pilkington
articles.description:
Brandon Herrera, a YouTuber known for making outrageous pro-gun statements, is the frontrunner to represent a district devastated by mass shootings
The video begins with Brandon Herrera staring intently into the camera. He is filming himself in a hotel room seated between twin beds, his black hair slicked back and beard neatly trimmed. He is wearing a T-shirt branded with his trademark nickname, “The AK Guy”, above the image of a semi-automatic rifle primed for action.
Three days earlier, on 3 August 2019, a white nationalist armed with a semi-automatic firearm not dissimilar to the one stamped across Herrera’s chest entered a busy Walmart store in the Texas border city of El Paso and opened fire.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nazi jokes and ‘cum trophies’: meet the Texas gunfluencer who could soon represent Uvalde

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Iran war, rising prices and president’s low ratings give Democrats advantage, but Republicans have poured cash into key races – could it be decisive?

Sign up for The Stakes 2026: your weekly guide to the US midterms

Donald Trump pulled out all the stops at the Republican party’s midterm convention two weeks ago. In speeches aimed at the voters who will soon decide whether to keep Republicans in control of Congress for the final phase of his presidency, the president dangled $5,000 checks, and warned the United States would turn into a “communist country” if Democrats are elected.
The unprecedented political gathering amounted to a Hail Mary pass at retaining control of Congress, which history indicated Trump’s Republican allies had always been likely to lose in the 3 November vote. Two weeks later, with election administrators in several states already sending out mail ballots, there is no indication the gambit has worked.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Republican jitters grow as unpopular Trump fuels midterm ‘bloodbath’ fears

articles.author: Amy Hawkins, and David Smith in Washington
articles.description:
Fears persist about Trump ‘sucking up’ to Xi on Taiwan, but few concrete outcomes anticipated from US meeting

AI, trade, Taiwan and climate: what will and won’t be on agenda at Trump-Xi summit

When Xi Jinping, China’s leader, touches down in Maryland on Wednesday, he will step out into the arms – perhaps a hug, if Donald Trump’s wishes come true – of a US president who has shown China more bonhomie than any of his recent predecessors.
The meeting between Xi and Trump this week will be the second time that the leaders of the world’s two biggest economies have talked face to face this year. At the previous summit, held in Beijing in May, there was much talk of building a “strategic stability” between the two powers. But there was little by way of concrete outcomes: the countries remain at loggerheads over trade, export controls and geopolitics.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: AI looms large over Trump-Xi meeting amid deep distrust between US and China

articles.author: Ted Widmer
articles.description:
Gone was any shred of US idealism. It was a spectacle of raw power – a power that is likely to only diminish in the years ahead
Expectations were low for Donald Trump’s address to the UN on Tuesday, and yet somehow it was even worse than expected. He does not perform well in formal settings, like chambers of government, preferring a blingier room, like Mar-a-Lago, or an outdoor rally. For years, he has made no secret of his hostility to the UN, and the very principles of international order that define it.
In recent years, that hostility has deepened into something more like a full-on assault, with frequent attacks on the international criminal court (perhaps out of fear that he will someday be indicted), on the UN’s climate agenda, and on Unesco (which the US decided to withdraw from in July 2025).
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump invades the UN with a brutish speech | Ted Widmer

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Jake and Logan Paul were invited to give a motivational speech. Just don’t let them get involved with military policy
We’re now approaching month seven of a war against Iran that Donald Trump repeatedly assured us would be over in a matter of weeks. Prices are rising, troop morale is plummeting, and there is little evidence things will improve.
The situation is so desperate that the decision makers at the Pentagon have decided to bring out the big guns. I’m not talking about nuclear weapons, although Trump recently threatened to “blow the entire nation [of Iran] up”. No, I’m talking about influencers Jake and Logan Paul, who are famous for doing idiotic stunts on YouTube and getting hit in the face during boxing matches. Last Thursday, Pete Hegseth’s Department of Defense or whatever they’re calling it these days (the Department of War Crimes?) welcomed the Paul brothers to Washington DC “to meet with our warriors” and deliver a motivational speech. In response, former Republican congressman and air force officer Adam Kinzinger wrote, “We aren’t a serious country at the moment.” That about sums it up.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Pentagon has unveiled its secret weapon: two idiotic influencers | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.description:
Protesters in Austin, Texas, demonstrated against the Trump administration’s hardline anti-immigration campaign after an ICE agent shot and wounded a man on Sunday afternoon. Eyewitness footage filmed moments after the shooting shows the ICE officer standing next to an open car door, in which there is a visible dent. The man, identified by relatives and his lawyer as 28-year-old Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, was taken to a hospital in Austin in a serious but stable condition, officials said, before being taken into custody.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, said it was leading an investigation into the officer involved in the shooting, with the help of the FBI. Austin police officers were not involved in the operation or the shooting, which occurred after a traffic stop, mayor Kirk Watson stated at a press conference 

ICE agent shoots and wounds Venezuelan man at traffic stop in Austin, Texas

articles.title: Protesters gather in Austin after ICE agent shoots and wounds man – video

articles.description:
Tech bosses have called for a slowdown in artificial intelligence and formal guardrails to be introduced by the US government. But President Trump is not moved by the doomsday predictions, calling them a ‘hoax'. What is behind his affection for the AI industry? Jonathan Freedland and Guardian US tech editor Blake Montgomery discuss
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Is Trump’s AI obsession walking the world into disaster? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman with Johana Bhuiyan . Produced by Tiara Chiaramonte engineered by Ivan Kuraev executive producers Jonathan Menjivar and Rachel Humphreys
articles.description:
A former Anthropic researcher’s apocalyptic declaration about artificial intelligence has led to a global panic that the technology might be the end of us all. At an event in Washington today to warn about the dangers of AI, US senator Bernie Sanders said that Congress has been ‘asleep at the wheel'. Oddly, Steve Bannon appeared at the same event. But is this response a distraction from the more immediate problems AI is already causing? Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian tech reporter Johana Bhuyian to put this moment in context, and she explains why we should be cynical about industry calls for regulation
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why the real AI apocalypse is already here – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Written by Oliver Bullough. Produced by Nicola Alexandrou. The executive producer was Ellie Bury
articles.description:
Hundreds of millions of pounds of dirty money are being deposited at post offices every year. So why are the police reluctant to investigate the scale of the problem?
By Oliver Bullough
Read the text version here
Support the Guardian today: theguardian.com/longreadpod
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The other Post Office scandal: how organised crime launders money on the high street – podcast

articles.author: Sarah Butler
articles.description:
Industry leaders call on government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security
The gap between Britain’s food and drink exports and imports has neared its highest this century, as a combination of Brexit, war in the Middle East and US tariffs dented deliveries overseas while imports soared.
The UK’s food and drink trade deficit has risen to more than £21bn – the largest since 2000 – in what industry leaders said was a “wake-up call” for the government to protect homegrown produce in the interest of national security.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK food and drink trade deficit largest since 2000 at £21bn

articles.author: Patrick Wintour in New York
articles.description:
Country says US must lift sanctions on its oil exports and end the war on all fronts, including in Lebanon
Iran said it has told Donald Trump it is willing to open the strait of Hormuz in six days, and to start talks on its nuclear program the day after, so long as the US lifts sanctions on Iran’s oil exports in return, ends the war on all fronts – including in Lebanon – and releases some of Iran’s frozen assets.
The proposal is designed to accelerate the steps first laid down in the memorandum of understanding signed by the US and Iran in June, particularly by helping the talks on Iran’s nuclear program start much more quickly than previously agreed.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Iran awaiting response from Trump on proposal to open strait of Hormuz in six days

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators 
Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise.
Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer

articles.author: Amelia Gentleman and Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Thirty-seven-year-old charged with one count of criminal damage and failing to disclose his phone pin to police 
The far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been charged with criminal damage and failing to disclose his phone pin to police following an incident in the Channel on Tuesday, where he allegedly slashed a dinghy while a French rescuer was on board.
Thomas, 37, of no fixed abode, has been charged with one count of criminal damage along with an offence under section 53 of the Regulation of Investigatory Powers Act 2000 (Ripa), for allegedly failing to comply with a notice to disclose a phone pin to police.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Far-right activist Daniel Thomas charged over alleged dinghy slashing in Channel

articles.author: Anna Bawden and Denis Campbell
articles.description:
Patient groups decry ‘scandalous’ delays as four integrated care boards take step due to soaring demand for diagnoses
NHS bodies are forcing people with suspected attention deficit hyperactivity disorder and autism to wait at least two years before they can be assessed as they struggle to meet surging demand for diagnoses of neurodiversity.
Four NHS integrated care boards (ICBs) covering large regions of England have adopted the approach because they cannot afford the cost of the number of assessments that people are seeking.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: NHS bodies in England impose two-year minimum wait for ADHD and autism assessments

articles.author: PA Media
articles.description:
Officers left feeling ‘hamstrung’, says Mark Rowley after offender allowed to return to flat overlooking playground
Pressure to cut the number of prisoners on remand has led to “dangerous and prolific offenders” being granted bail, the country’s most senior police officer said after a paedophile was allowed to return to his flat that overlooked a children’s playground.
Zafer Dogan was jailed on Thursday for two years and four months after he was convicted of taking thousands of pictures of women and girls before using AI technology to turn them into nude images for his sexual gratification.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Met chief criticises court system after paedophile granted bail

articles.author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
articles.description:
Warnings about the catastrophic effects of vital ecosystems collapsing were not published under previous PM

UK shares findings of damning climate crisis national security report suppressed under Starmer

UK spy chiefs warned government ministers of the catastrophic impacts on national security from the collapse of vital ecosystems around the world, driven by the climate crisis and the overexploitation of nature. But their report, which was supposed to be published almost a year ago, was suppressed under Keir Starmer. Now the government is briefing foreign ministers from other countries on the findings, with a view to gathering global support for more concerted action on the risks.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why is the UK’s suppressed climate national security report significant?

articles.author: Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Monthly ‘thank you’ payments for people hosting refugees to be cut from £350 to £100 from next year
Ukrainian refugees in the UK fear they could be left homeless after the government quietly axed 70% of funding for hosts of the Homes for Ukraine scheme, reducing monthly “thank you” payments to them from £350 to £100.
The scheme was launched after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has provided support for 181,000 of the 234,000 Ukrainians who have since sought sanctuary in the UK.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ukrainians in UK fear homelessness over host scheme funding cuts

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels
articles.description:
‘If you’re not in the internal market, you don’t get the same protection,’ says French minister of policy designed to curb Chinese competition
France is leading a push to exclude the UK from the EU’s “Made in Europe” policy that could result in British companies losing out in the race to supply European countries with low-carbon technologies and electric cars.
The plans were raised by Andy Burnham when he met the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, on the sidelines of the UN general assembly earlier this week.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France says EU’s ‘Made in Europe’ law should not include the UK

articles.author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
articles.description:
Datacentre hailed by government was supposed to start operating next year but may be held back into mid-2030s
A huge datacentre project hailed by the UK government will miss its launch date next year and could be delayed into the mid-2030s.
The site in Loughton, Essex, was described as the country’s largest AI supercomputer when it was announced in 2025, but power supply problems mean it now faces a lengthy wait before coming online.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Launch of UK’s ‘largest AI supercomputer’ delayed by power supply problems

articles.author: Guardian community team
articles.description:
There were 13,464 reported assaults against passengers and members of the public on the mainline railway in 2025-26
The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has risen to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year, data published by the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) shows.
There were 13,464 reported assaults against passengers and members of the public on the mainline railway in 2025-26, up 36% on the previous year and the highest number recorded by the ORR since it started tracking the figures in 2004.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tell us: have you been assaulted on Great Britain’s railways?

articles.author: Gwyn Topham Transport correspondent
articles.description:
Unions say record high of nearly 25,000, including assaults on rail workers and public, shows need for more staff and policing

Tell us: have you been assaulted on Great Britain’s railways?

The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has risen by a fifth to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year.
Unions said the “horrendous” figures showed the need for more staff and policing, as the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) revealed a sharp increase in assaults on the travelling public and on railway staff last year.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways rise by fifth in a year

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
TV heads hope the revamped show – back after four decades – will win over parents seeking quality shows amid concerns about addictive online content
For the generations who grew up watching Humpty, Jemima and Big Ted, the mere mention of the BBC’s Play School evokes a pang of childhood nostalgia.
The show, which featured much-loved presenters such as Floella Benjamin and Johnny Ball, became synonymous with wholesome children’s television during its run of more than 20 years on air.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ready to knock? Play School returns as BBC pushes quality children’s programming

articles.author: Jillian Ambrose Energy correspondent
articles.description:
US president’s suggested 90-day export ban before midterm elections could bring even higher fuel prices across Europe
The EU has warned Donald Trump against plans to ban US diesel exports to the global market, saying the move would negatively affect Europe and the US.
The European Commission has reacted with “concern” to reports this week that the US president could prevent diesel from reaching the global market.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: EU says Trump plan to ban US diesel exports would ‘negatively impact both sides’

articles.description:
MoD claims book by soldier known as Christian Craighead contains alleged breach of confidentiality contract
An injunction preventing a former member of the SAS from publishing a book about his role in a counter-terrorism operation has been extended after an application by the Ministry of Defence.
The block on publication of the book in the UK will continue until the conclusion of a government legal action against the soldier, who is known only by the pseudonym Christian Craighead.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Injunction blocking publication of ex-SAS soldier’s book on counter-terror op extended

articles.author: Heather Stewart and Graeme Wearden
articles.description:
Treasury sources concede ‘less room’ for manoeuvre as global bond selloff also hikes government’s borrowing costs

International bodies warn of rising debt and borrowing risks

Burnham stands by claim UK is ‘in hock’ to bond markets


Oil prices lurched upwards again on Thursday, creating a growing headache for UK policymakers ahead of John Healey’s budget next month.
While Healey has been keen to present an upbeat picture of the UK’s economic prospects, Treasury sources concede the sharp jump in oil and gas prices means they have “less room” than a month ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil price rise creates more pressure on UK policymakers before budget

articles.author: Julia Kollewe
articles.description:
Online electricals retailer says latest purchase continues to broaden its appeal beyond white goods, phones and TV
The troubled camera retailer Jessops has changed hands after AO World acquired the business from the Dragons’ Den star Peter Jones.
The online electrical retailer said on Thursday it had completed the acquisition of Jessops.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Flash sale: AO snaps up camera seller Jessops from Dragons’ Den star Peter Jones

articles.author: Rachel Hall and Patrick Greenfield
articles.description:
Role for Anant Ambani, son of India’s richest person, who also runs a controversial mega-zoo, met with incredulity
Newcastle University is facing a backlash from conservationists over the appointment of the heir to an Indian oil and gas fortune who runs a controversial mega-zoo as a professor of sustainability.
The university announced that Anant Ambani had been given a professorship of practice for “his work in conservation, biodiversity protection, animal welfare and environmental stewardship” and “significant contributions to advancing a more sustainable future”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Backlash as Indian oil heir made professor of sustainability by Newcastle University

articles.author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
articles.description:
Duo had US hits with their cover of Always Something There to Remind Me as well as Promises, Promises and more
Pete Byrne, the frontman of British new wave group Naked Eyes who carried them to repeated chart successes in the US, has died aged 74.
The news was announced on the band’s website and social media on Wednesday, stating that Byrne died peacefully in Los Angeles on 14 September after a brief illness.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Pete Byrne, frontman of British new wave band Naked Eyes, dies aged 74

articles.author: Rachel Hall
articles.description:
Former deputy PM now involved in tech industry says many within sector are ‘winding themselves up into a lather’
Nick Clegg has dismissed fears over AI’s “godlike power to exterminate humanity”, calling it a sign that tech bosses are “breathing their own fumes”.
The former UK deputy prime minister said that tech bosses should focus on addressing known specific threats such as cybersecurity and bioweapons rather than the “slightly hand-wavy view that this technology is unavoidably going to develop some godlike power which is going to turn on us and exterminate humanity”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nick Clegg plays down fears ‘godlike’ AI could exterminate humanity

articles.author: Ashley Kirk and Jessica Elgot. Illustrations by Prina Shah
articles.description:
Analysis reveals groups with sharply contrasting priorities – and who has drifted the most from Labour towards Greens and Reform
• Tactical voting at next election could push Reform into fourth place, poll finds
A new MRP poll suggests Labour would remain the largest party if a general election were held now, but would fall well short of an overall majority as Reform surged into second place.
Behind those headline figures, research from Survation and 38 Degrees casts new light on five distinct voter groups who are collectively defined as the “progressive majority”. These people share concerns about living costs and the NHS, but differ over immigration, the environment, political trust and the pace of change needed to address the UK’s policies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From idealists to struggling sceptics: how Labour’s majority depends on five progressive voter types – in charts

articles.author: Jessica Elgot and Ashley Kirk
articles.description:
Polling suggests Andy Burnham is attracting progressives back to Labour, motivated by desire to stop Nigel Farage
• How Labour’s majority depends on five progressive voter types – in charts
Progressive voters could push Reform UK into fourth place and put Labour within touching distance of a majority if tactical voting is widespread at the next election, a major poll has found.
Andy Burnham is beginning to attract a significant number of left-leaning voters back to Labour, motivated by a desire to stop Nigel Farage, the results suggest.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tactical voting at next election could push Reform into fourth place, poll finds

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
IPPR finds failure to align testing standards has forced companies to abandon exporting to EU and is costing costing 0.18% of national income
The UK is losing out on annual exports to the EU that could be worth as much as £6.5bn without a deal with Brussels that allows manufacturers to jettison duplicate product testing.
In the latest attempt to calculate the loss of trade with the EU after Brexit, the IPPR thinktank said many companies have given up selling goods to the EU or set up subsidiaries inside the trade bloc after successive governments failed to secure a mutual recognition agreement that would avoid the extra administration costs.
Motor vehicle and part exports would have been between £2.48bn and £3.42bn higher each year.
Electronic exports could have been between £1.17bn and £1.67bn higher.
Pharmaceutical exports would have had an estimated annual uplift of between £740m and £820m.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK ‘losing up to £6.5bn a year in EU trade’ without post-Brexit product deal

An RAF jet crashed and exploded moments after two pilots ejected during a training flight over Anglesey (Ynys Môn), in north Wales, on Wednesday.

The Hawk T2 had just taken off from RAF Valley on the west of the island when the incident occurred, witnesses said. Both pilots parachuted to the ground and were reportedly treated for minor injuries


RAF jet crashes and explodes in Anglesey moments after pilots eject

articles.title: RAF pilots eject from training plane before crash – video

articles.author: Sandra Laville
articles.description:
Exclusive: Levy that allows almost 16,000 houses to be built on Norfolk Broads will not cover cost of mitigating environmental damage, critics say
A new levy on developers to allow almost 16,000 homes to be built in the environmentally protected Norfolk Broads has been cut by tens of thousands of pounds per house, the Guardian can reveal.
Ministers say the government’s environmental delivery plans (EDPs) were created to unblock housing growth across the country and are a “win-win” for development and nature.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Cash to trash’ levy on house developers too low to offset damage to Norfolk Broads, say critics

articles.author: Andrew Gregory and Will Parman
articles.description:
Approach to treating high blood pressure ‘not fit for purpose’, say researchers, with 59% of cases undiagnosed
Only half of people being treated by a GP for high blood pressure in England have it under control, and millions more are completely unaware they have the “silent killer” condition, research reveals.
Most people with hypertension (59%) are in the dark and undiagnosed, raising their risk of stroke, heart attack and early death, according to the largest ever study of its kind.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millions in England unaware they have ‘silent killer’ high blood pressure, research reveals

articles.author: Dan Milmo and Robert Booth
articles.description:
Whether produced by Russia, China or far-right influencers, deepfakes and disinfo are pushing multiple false narratives
Russian disinformation campaigns are varied in their falsehoods and strategies.
The narratives range from a deepfake Tom Cruise criticising the Paris Olympics to portraying a recent Russian attack on a train near the Ukraine-Poland border as a false-flag operation.
 Continue reading...

articles.author: Karen McVeigh
articles.description:
Cooperation on OceanEye, which aims to create ‘real-time’ model of world’s oceans, comes amid efforts to boost EU ties
Britain is to join a major new ocean science programme, led by the EU, to better forecast extreme weather and climate events, the environment secretary is to announce in New York.
The announcement on Wednesday will come as Andy Burnham’s government aims to rebuild the UK’s relationship with Europe, and follows warnings this year’s “supersized” El Niño, tracked in the Pacific Ocean, will fuel more extreme weather globally.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK to join EU ocean science scheme to better predict extreme weather events

articles.author: Matthew Pearce
articles.description:
Author Russell Warfield argues the Green leader’s brand of politics is not new but has evolved in the party over time 
Watermelons: the term used to describe the members of the Green party of England and Wales who are green on the outside and red on the inside. People in this faction are environmentalists but bleed socialist ideologies.
Of the roughly 160,000 people who have flocked to the party since Zack Polanski became leader last year, most are thought to be in this camp, drawn to a political space on the left that they see as vacated by the Labour party.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Watermelons’: Zack Polanski and the rise of the ‘green outside, red inside’ eco-populists

articles.author: Eve Livingston Scotland correspondent
articles.description:
Eleven per cent increase in fatalities last year partly down to presence of nitazenes in Scotland’s illicit drug market
New forms of a powerful synthetic opioid have contributed to a sharp rise in Scottish drug deaths, with the latest data showing an 11% increase in fatalities last year
Annual figures released by National Records of Scotland (NRS) on Wednesday recorded 1,133 drug-related deaths in 2025, 116 more than the previous year. The 2025 figures are the sixth highest on record.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New powerful synthetic opioids behind sharp rise in Scottish drug deaths

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
NHS England initiative to reduce cut-off period to three months ‘disproportionately affecting’ most deprived areas
An NHS policy to remove “ghost patients” from GP lists is inadvertently leaving some of the poorest people in England without vital healthcare, analysis has found.
Under previous NHS rules, inactive patients at risk of being removed from their GP practice were given six months to respond to outreach. But under NHS England’s accelerated list validation timeline, introduced last October, patients now have only three months to reply.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Ghost patient’ policy wrongly removing at-risk people from GP lists, doctors say

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
Exclusive: Restoration work at Bath Assembly Rooms unearths Roman ditches containing pottery, coins and fragments of a military helmet
The restoration of a Georgian building in Bath once frequented by Jane Austen has unexpectedly provided a tantalising glimpse into the life of the city’s Roman suburbanites.
A network of Roman ditches containing pottery, coins, glassware and a fragment of a military helmet has been found beneath Bath Assembly Rooms in the north of the city.

Entire £253m budget for 2026 allocated in less than a day, leaving thousands of farmers disappointed
Thousands of farmers have been left empty-handed with the government’s 2026 nature funding spent in just six hours.
The £253m sustainable farming incentive (SFI) scheme opened for applications from farmers at 10am on Tuesday.
This article was corrected on 23 Sept 2026: an earlier version said the budget was £233m, but in fact it was for £253m, after Defra allocated an additional £20m.

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent

Party strategists say careful targeting of seats has paid off and should continue, but some say a wider vision is needed
One of the more dramatic moments in a Liberal Democrat conference otherwise short of them came late on Sunday, when the party frontbencher Lisa Smart told the polling veteran John Curtice that, in effect, he no longer understood modern politics.
Curtice had warned the Lib Dems they risked being left behind, with the lack of a coherent national message seeing them all but ignored outside a few electoral strongholds. Smart’s response? In the new era of five- or six-party politics, and mass tactical voting, this does not matter.

PM hopes to be firmer with US leader than his predecessor without provoking diplomatic warfare, as the Iran war weighs on the UK economy
No international relationship has more power to determine the success of Andy Burnham’s premiership. So you might imagine the stakes for the prime minister’s first face-to-face meeting with Donald Trump on Tuesday would be high.

Community groups and schools work with Wales’s folk arts organisation to set  stories of the area’s people to music
Growing up in Wales, Liz Puleston-Jones was familiar with the country’s rich heritage of storytelling and traditional music, but none of it ever seemed to have much of a connection to her life in Swansea.
Researching the history of the area as part of Cân y Cymoedd (When Valleys Sing), a project in nearby Port Talbot, she came across the story of Isabel Thomas, a 14-year-old girl in the 1940s who left school and lied about her age to work in a tin plate works to support her family.

Rhys Woods says there are ‘no words’ for family’s pain after Noah’s body was found in pond near Suffolk playground
The father of Noah, the three-year-old boy who was found dead after going missing from a playground, has spoken of his heartbreak and thanked the community who launched a tireless search for his son.

Frontier AI now has capability to expose those vulnerabilities at a rate quicker than we can keep up, quicker than we can patch them.
